articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Designation Information
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an update to its Iran designation information on November 9, 2026.

Further details regarding the specific entities or individuals affected by this update were not immediately available, but such actions typically involve modifications to existing entries on the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List or other sanctions lists.
These updates are part of ongoing efforts to maintain the integrity and effectiveness of U.S. sanctions programs against Iran.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates New Entities in Iran-Related Sanctions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026.

These designations target individuals and entities involved in activities that support Iran's destabilizing behavior, including its proliferation of weapons of mass destruction or its support for terrorism.
The action aims to further restrict Iran's access to the international financial system and pressure the regime to alter its policies.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Cyber and Transnational Criminal Organization Designations, Issues Cuba-Related Actions
body: On November 5, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting cyber-related activities and transnational criminal organizations.
Concurrently, OFAC issued new designations related to Cuba and published a Cuba-related determination.
These actions underscore the U.S. government's commitment to combating malicious cyber activities, disrupting criminal networks, and enforcing sanctions against the Cuban regime.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces New Iran-Related Designations, Updates Venezuela General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) implemented new Iran-related designations and updated certain Iran-related listings on November 4, 2026.
In conjunction with these actions, OFAC published an Iran-related alert and issued an amended Venezuela-related General License along with a new Frequently Asked Question.
These measures aim to tighten sanctions enforcement against Iran while providing updated guidance for Venezuela-related transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License.
This amendment modifies existing authorizations for certain transactions involving Iran, providing updated guidance to ensure compliance with U.S. sanctions policy.
The specific details of the amendments were made available on the Treasury website.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities Related to North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo on October 28, 2026.
These actions aim to counter illicit activities supporting the North Korean regime and address human rights abuses and corruption in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The designations underscore the U.S. commitment to global security and human rights.

articles.headline: OFAC Reaches Settlement Agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc.
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. on October 27, 2026.
The settlement addresses apparent violations of OFAC sanctions regulations, highlighting the importance of robust compliance programs for companies operating internationally.
Further details of the violations and the terms of the settlement were published on the OFAC website.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions, Filing Reports
body: On October 26, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments provide updated guidance for financial institutions and other entities on their obligations under OFAC regulations.
The revised FAQs aim to clarify compliance requirements and streamline reporting processes.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026.

Concurrently, OFAC removed certain entities from its Belarus and North Korea designations, and issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses, along with amended Frequently Asked Questions.
These actions reflect a dynamic approach to sanctions, adjusting measures based on ongoing geopolitical developments and policy objectives.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations and Issues Associated General Licenses
body: On October 19, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA).
In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued associated General Licenses to provide guidance and authorization for certain related transactions.
These actions aim to protect American intellectual property from theft and illicit exploitation.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
